rationale: The current topology suffers from excessive power consumption (IDD = 17.39 mA vs 5 mA max), poor gain (S21 = 6.2 dB vs 16 dB min), and slightly degraded NF (2.036 dB vs 2.0 dB max), with the most negative normalized margin in NF. The primary issue stems from insufficient transconductance and improper impedance matching due to a lack of proper input matching network and a poorly structured cascode or source-degeneration path. To improve the NF and S21 while reducing Idd, we must enhance input matching and increase gain via a cascode structure with an inductor in the source path to boost output impedance and stabilize gain. Replacing the single NMOS M1 with a cascode NMOS pair (M1 + M2) and inserting a source inductor Ls to provide inductive peaking and better impedance matching at 5.8 GHz will improve S21 and NF, while reducing the required bias current due to better transconductance efficiency. This edit directly targets the binding constraints (NF and S21) without worsening S11 or increasing Idd excessively.
